title: Tom Ballard's iPad Mini 4: a month from a rut to Omarchy A
summary: Tom Ballard, who writes Today in Omarchy, spent a month of commutes getting Omarchy onto an 11-year-old iPad Mini 4, with help from Henrik Klee's Orchard tools. On 26 November he posted that Omarchy A runs on it.

topics.angle: How far people will carry it: a device Apple calls unsupportable.

claims.text: On 24 October Tom said he was in a rut trying to get Omarchy running on the iPad Mini 4.
On 26 October, on a three hour morning commute, the iPad booted native Linux over one USB cable, into RAM, with the internal storage untouched.
Tom thanked Henrik Klee for helping with Henrik's Orchard command line tool.
By 30 October the iPad, 11 years old, played Tom's Omarchy snake video at 60 fps.
On 2 November Tom posted that Omarchy ran on the iPad Mini 4.
On 4 November it booted Omarchy in 12 seconds with no failed services, and touch was accurate to about 1 mm.
Tom took a weekend off and wrote: turns out I can leave the laptop shut.
On 16 November he was back to the GPU work on the commute.
On 26 November Omarchy A ran on the iPad Mini 4. Tom credits Henrik Klee and the community, and wrote that Apple decided it was unsupportable hardware.
Omarchy A describes itself as an experimental, Omarchy-inspired desktop for Apple A-series devices, built on Arch Linux ARM and reworked for touch.
The Omarchy A README lists iPad Air 2, iPad 5 to 7 and iPhone 7 to X as compatible; the iPad Mini 4 is not on that list.
